intro.say:
## Where we are

I read `app.py`. Signup validates email with a hand-written regex. It accepts `a@b` and rejects `first+tag@example.com`. The tests in `test_app.py` only cover the happy path.

checkpoint.question: How should we handle email validation?

options.label: Tighten the email regex and add tests for the edge cases it currently accepts
Replace the hand-written regex with a maintained validation library
Leave validation as it is and move on to the retry bug

regex.say: I tightened the regex and added five edge-case tests. Four pass. `first+tag@example.com` still fails, because the pattern rejects `+` in the local part.

checkpoint.question: The plus-address test still fails. What next?

options.label: Allow + in the local part and rerun the tests
Drop the plus-address test; it is out of scope

library.say: I swapped the regex for `email-validator`. All existing tests pass. The library also does a DNS lookup by default, which makes the tests hit the network.

checkpoint.question: The library makes network calls in tests. What next?

options.label: Turn off the DNS check and keep the library

retry.say: Leaving validation alone. The retry bug is in `send_welcome`: it retries on every exception, including bad input.

done.say: Done. That is the end of this session.
